newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo internal probe taking longer than expected.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo internal probe taking longer than expected.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp's internal probe of massive copper market losses is taking longer than initially expected, due partly to a lack of cooperation from counterparties to loss-making trades, Sumitomo president Kenji Miyahara said on Monday.

"We must minutely scrutinise massive and complex transactions over 10 years, and for reasons such as the fact that we are not receiving sufficient cooperation from the counterparties, the progress of the investigation is taking longer than we expected," Miyahara said in a statement.
He did not specify whether the counterparties were refusing or simply unable to cooperate with the investigation.
Sumitomo has accused its former chief copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka of amassing $2.6 billion in losses from unauthorised trading over a 10-year period.
Hamanaka was fired last June and was later charged by Tokyo prosecutors with forgery and fraud in connection with the losses.
"At the end of last year Hamanaka was charged with forgery and fraud, marking a milestone in this case, but our internal investigation is still underway," Miyahara said.
"Investigations by the British and U.S. authorities are also continuing, and we continue to cooperate with them," he added.

"At present, in our internal investigation, we are reconstructing and tracing Hamanaka's transactions, making the greatest possible efforts to clarify all the facts of the case, such as what methods were used to get around company rules and on what points our systems of checks were inadequate," he said.
"We want to complete the investigation as quickly as possible and clarify policies and steps that the company should take to prevent a recurrence," he said.
